title: Six-round lower bound for linear-schedule IEM under full XRKA
summary: Decide whether any linearly scheduled IEM with a two-block master key needs at least six rounds to beat the birthday bound under full XOR-related-key attacks.

formal_statement.body: Let an IEM use public random $n$-bit permutations and derive every round key linearly over XOR from a uniformly random $2n$-bit master key. In the adaptive bidirectional full-$\Phi_{\mathrm{XOR}}$ related-key experiment, prove that beyond-birthday security requires at least six rounds, or refute the claim by giving an at-most-five-round construction with a compatible security proof.

scope.domain: Linear-key-schedule iterated Even--Mansour ciphers under full XOR-induced related-key attacks.
assumptions: All round keys are linear functions of the master key over XOR.
Independent public random $n$-bit permutations and adaptive bidirectional oracle access.
scope.unresolved_remainder: No proof of the universal six-round lower bound and no full-XRKA-secure construction with at most five rounds was found.

progress.summary: The source conjectures that a $2n$-bit linear key schedule needs at least six IEM rounds for beyond-birthday full-XRKA security.
